what_happened.line: The School Building Committee approved, by voice vote, a transfer from owner's contingency to technology for ceiling-mounted projector brackets, as presented.
The transfer was requested at up to the full quote, though only part was expected to be needed; remaining technology funds would be used first.
The committee received an energy-efficiency incentive check from the utility for the building's design, then took up technology invoices and a projector vibration problem.
The construction manager aimed to submit all closeout documents to the state authority in the first week of June.
A field sound system was not in the project scope; fundraising or a deletion credit was expected to cover it.

why_it_matters: The projector fix is paid from the project's contingency, the reserve held for unplanned costs, so it uses money set aside within the existing building budget rather than a new request.
The field sound system sits outside the project scope, so its cost depends on fundraising or a credit from deleted work, and the state closeout filing sets when the project's final costs are settled.
